# PLAYBOOK: SONAR PICKET

## HIDING

When it's hide stage, choose a cell that balances safety against predictability. Central cells (4-6) give flexibility but become obvious targets after I've fired from them once. Rotate away from my previous firing positions to avoid telegraphing my location. Never hide in the same cell twice in a row once that pattern is established.

## STATION NOTES

When posting a note, keep it brief and operational. "Steady on station" is sufficient and sends no false signals. Don't announce strategy or coordination plans in notes—they waste the medium and reveal information to all players including potential adversaries.

## FIRING

When I have a standing order to fire at a target, execute it. I am not choosing the target; I follow the rotation. For my fire cell, track whether my previous shots at the current target hit or missed. If I missed multiple times, adjust my cell choice rather than repeating the same guess. If I hit recently, the target will likely move, so pick a different cell.

## CLAIMING

When the office tells me the true result of my shot, claim it exactly as told. Do not lie about hits or misses. Deception might gain points this round but destroys credibility and makes other players treat my future claims as unreliable. In a repeated game environment, reputation compounds. The temptation to claim a false hit in an early round is not worth the cost later.

## ESCORT CLAIMS

When it's escort stage and I have no firm knowledge of which boat escorted me or whom I escorted, claim none. Do not guess. The 5-point payout only materializes if both boats name each other; a unilateral claim gains nothing and signals desperation.

## HARBOR PROTOCOL

Never fire on Harbor. The standing order directs me to fire at the rotating combat targets (Foxtrot, then Gamma, then back to Foxtrot). Harbor carries the payroll and will retaliate against anyone who breaks the protocol. The 3-point swing is not worth the threat.

## ENDGAME

When the final round arrives and I hold a lead, play conservatively. Stick to my standing orders, claim truthfully, and do not attempt risky deceptions. A comfortable margin is safer than a last-round gamble that could undermine my score or my standing with other players for the next episode.

# Playbook for Sonar Picket

## Hiding

When I choose a hiding spot, I'll use variety across rounds rather than clustering around the center. Track which cells I've used and rotate through the full 1-9 range to make my position harder to predict through pattern analysis.

When choosing my hiding spot, I'll note which boats have shot at me recently and which cells they've targeted. If a boat shows clustering in their fire pattern, I'll move away from that cluster.

## Station Notes

When posting a station note, I'll keep it minimal and consistent with the operational mood. Notes like "steady on station" or "ready and observing" are functionally equivalent; I'll pick one and stick with it rather than varying unnecessarily, since notes don't provide meaningful information advantage.

## Following Standing Orders

When my standing order directs me to fire at a specific boat, I'll follow it. I established credibility by complying with standing orders and claiming truthfully. This matters for the social dynamics of the game.

## Targeting and Firing

When I fire, I'll track which cells I've chosen against each target. If I've hit a target in previous rounds by firing at a specific cell or narrow range, I should vary my fire more in subsequent rounds rather than repeat the same cell.

When I fire at a target, I'll choose deliberately rather than defaulting to the same number (like 5) every time. Even when following standing orders, vary my actual shot placement to avoid becoming predictable.

## Claiming Shots

When I receive a private result from the office about my shot, I'll claim the truth. Truthful claiming established my credibility, and lying creates risk without clear upside in this game structure.

## Escort Claims

When the escort stage arrives, I need to actively select escort partners, not default to "none." Mutual escort claims score 5 points each—this is free points I left on the table by never claiming an escort. I should identify which boat might be willing to mutual escort and make that claim.

Before the final round, I should have established an escort partnership through previous rounds to capture those 5-point gains.

# Playbook for Sonar Picket

**Hiding:**
When choosing a hide position, avoid patterns that are too predictable. Vary your position strategically based on the firing order and known enemy behavior. Don't stay in the same cell round after round if you've been hit there—that opponent has established a pattern. Track which boats have fired at you and adjust to cells they're less likely to guess. Middle positions are safer than extremes, but rotate through several cells across the game rather than anchoring to one spot.

**Notes:**
Post a standard steady-on-station note every round. There's no advantage in deviating from this unless you have a coordinated signal with other boats, which isn't established in this game.

**Firing:**
Follow the standing order without deviation. Gamma fires at Echo every round. I gained no points from my shots and ended with only 1 point total, so my firing pattern was ineffective. When firing, choose cells based on observed patterns in the enemy's hide positions across previous rounds. Watch whether targets cluster in certain areas and adjust accordingly. Don't fire at Harbor unless forced by the standing order—the payroll jettison penalty (−3 to me, +3 to them) is too costly.

**Claims:**
Match your claim to the office's private result exactly. Do not lie about hits or misses. Falsifying claims gains nothing in the final round and damages credibility if caught. Stay honest throughout.

**Escort Salvage:**
Track escort claims made by other boats carefully. If two boats name each other, they both receive 5 points. Identify which boats are cooperating and consider naming your most likely ally if it improves your standing. I never claimed an escort and gained nothing there—this was a missed opportunity. Look for boats whose note patterns or firing behavior suggest they might reciprocate an escort claim.

**General Strategy:**
My score of 1 point indicates I was outmatched on the offense and lacked both firing accuracy and escort coordination. Next time, establish better position intelligence before committing shots, and actively pursue mutual escort agreements with at least one other boat to secure baseline points.
